commits.edited_message:
set alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering

VP8InitDithering() now sets dec->alpha_dithering for any alpha plane,
not just level-quantized ones: whether the levels actually need
smoothing is only known once the alpha header has been parsed, so the
check now uses ALPHDecoder::pre_processing at the smoothing site in
VP8DecompressAlphaRows() instead of peeking at the raw alpha header
byte a second time.

Also only decode all alpha rows in one pass in VP8DecompressAlphaRows
when dec->alpha_dithering > 0.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.

The full plane only needs to stay resident while it can still be
smoothed as a whole, which WebPDequantizeLevels() only does for a
level-quantized alpha plane; any other alpha plane is emitted row by
row and only needs the sliding window.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

coupling: The defect emerges only from the composition of the two edited commits around the alpha-dithering flag semantics. Commit c5a8cf0 (set alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering) widens dec->alpha_dithering: it is now set whenever any alpha plane is present, deferring the level-quantized (ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS) test to the smoothing site in VP8DecompressAlphaRows(), where ALPHDecoder::pre_processing is used after ALPHInit(). Read alone this is a benign refactor: at that point in history alpha memory is still allocated unconditionally at full height, so the widened flag only means the one-pass decode path is taken a bit more often, into a buffer that is always big enough. Commit 0e8d4fc (use sliding window for decoded alpha rows) then narrows the alpha allocation: WebPGetAlphaWindowRows() keeps the full plane resident only for a level-quantized alpha plane (the only case where WebPDequantizeLevels() smooths the image as a whole) and allocates a ~25+16+MAX_LENGTH/width-row sliding window otherwise. Read alone this is also benign: with the flag semantics that commit was written against, alpha_dithering>0 implied the alpha plane was level-quantized, so whenever VP8DecompressAlphaRows() decoded the whole plane in one pass (num_rows = height - row), the full-height buffer was still allocated. Composed, the two edits diverge: for a plain (non-quantized) alpha plane with alpha_dithering_strength > 0 requested, commit c5a8cf0's widened flag drives the one-pass branch (num_rows = height) while commit 0e8d4fc's narrowed allocation provides only the sliding window (for a 64x512 image, ~156 rows instead of 512), so the row-by-row unfilter loop in ALPHDecode() memcpy's past the end of dec->alpha_plane (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE in NoneUnfilter_C via ALPHDecode -> VP8DecompressAlphaRows -> FinishRow). A correct fix must reason across both commits: either the flag semantics in VP8InitDithering/VP8DecompressAlphaRows must again guarantee that dithering>0 implies a level-quantized plane, or the allocation in WebPGetAlphaWindowRows must again cover every case in which the one-pass decode is taken. Fixing only commit c5a8cf0's diff (restore the LEVELS gate on the flag) leaves a working tree that is merely equivalent to the original batch, and fixing only commit 0e8d4fc's diff (size by alpha_dithering again) leaves the widened flag from c5a8cf0 driving the one-pass decode against the window allocation - each single-commit fix removes the crash only by happenstance of re-coupling the invariant that the other commit still breaks; neither single diff contains both the producer (one-pass decode keyed on the widened flag) and the consumer (window-sized allocation keyed on the narrowed predicate) of the mismatch.

pocs.entry_point: WebPDecode (webp/decode.h) with config.options.alpha_dithering_strength=100, MODE_RGBA; embedded byte-for-byte in pocs/probe.c
